title: Data Analyst Roadmap
summary: Build from programming, statistics and business fundamentals into SQL, Excel, Python, BI, experimentation and business-focused data analysis.

facts.Timeline assumption: Four-year B.Tech/B.E. beginning in 2026 and completing around 2030. Each semester should produce a measurable skill or portfolio artifact.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: establish SQL, Excel, statistics, Python and BI capability with business-focused projects.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: specialise in product analytics, business intelligence, marketing analytics, finance analytics or operations analytics.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: move toward senior analytics, analytics engineering, data science or analytics leadership.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: combine analytics with AI-assisted analysis, experimentation, data products, business strategy and decision systems.

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

If your institution offers a four-year honours route, use the additional depth for an analytics capstone, business research project, internship or analytics-engineering project rather than simply adding more introductory certifications.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Move beyond dashboard creation toward analytical problem solving, experimentation, data modelling, automation and decision support. AI can accelerate analysis, but analysts still need to validate data quality, assumptions, statistical reasoning and business context.

blocks.label: Career progression

blocks.text: PhD routes

Keep moving from reporting toward decision systems. Strong senior analysts combine statistical reasoning, experimentation, data engineering awareness, business strategy and AI-assisted analysis. Domain expertise can become as important as another programming language.
